answer: One rented server can spin up 1,000 clones, each claiming a plot in the garden — unless identity is tied to hardware. Each agent must present a TPM attestation quote: signed proof from a secure chip on distinct physical silicon, rooted in one place like a juniper, not copyable to a VM. The quote cannot be cloned, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 chips, not one cloud account. That defeats container cloning outright. Trade-off: plain-VM agents are excluded until they get attested hardware, and trust shifts to chip makers. A yarrow patch of rented devices could sprout, but each stem costs a device.
